samples.question: This picture shows one head drawn as a large solid light-coloured disc on a plain light background. Inside the head there are exactly three dark marks: two small solid round dots, which are the eyes, and one long curved stroke, which is the mouth. The thin grey outline of the head, the thin grey frame near the edge of the picture and any short grey ticks are decoration and never indicate the answer. Now imagine the straight line that joins the two ends of the mouth stroke: the middle of the mouth stroke lies to one side of that straight line, and that is the side it bulges to. The head is drawn at an arbitrary rotation, so the eyes may appear below, beside or above the mouth on the page, and the head's size, position and colours, the size and spacing of the eyes, and the length and thickness of the mouth stroke all change from picture to picture. The face need not be drawn the way faces are usually drawn. Read only what is painted in this picture and do not answer from how faces usually look. Does the middle of the mouth stroke bulge toward the eyes or away from the eyes? Answer with exactly one of: toward, away.
